svg.title: Seal and Decision Clocks Relators Should Expect
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-04-seal-and-decision-clocks; chapter number: 2; chart type: horizontal_bars; title: Seal and Decision Clocks Relators Should Expect; subtitle: Reported ranges for seal renewals, total seal time, and case resolution; unit: months; caption: Seals renew 6 months at a time, total periods of 8 months, 14 months, or a couple of years are common, and many cases finish two or three years after filing.; assumptions note: Years converted to months (a couple of years shown as 24); where no point estimate was quoted, typical marks the lower bound of the stated range.; note: Sources: Stephen Teller - Teller Law (SiATzxJHy2Y), Phillips & Cohen LLP (5-ptDaAQkvI), Tycko & Zavareei LLP (Jon Tycko, A2nRu5da_9k).; bars: label: Seal renewal increment; min: 6; max: 6; typical: 6; display: 6 months at a time (Teller); label: Total seal periods reported; min: 8; max: 24; typical: 14; display: 8, 14, or about 24 months (Teller); label: Filing to case finish; min: 24; max: 36; typical: 24; display: 2 to 3 years (Teller); label: DOJ intervention decision; min: 11; max: 11; typical: 11; display: About 11 months average (Phillips & Cohen); label: Customs seal average; min: 18; max: 18; typical: 18; display: About 18 months (Tycko)
